name: Hong Kong action
summary: Action built in the cut and in the body: slow motion, wide anamorphic frames and a stunt shot in full view. Gunfights are choreographed like dance, and fights are made of clear, fast phrases.

philosophy.core_thesis: An action scene is a piece of choreography shot and cut for its rhythm, so the stunt is shown whole and the cut gives it speed and weight.
design_principles: Shoot the stunt in a wide or medium shot that shows the whole body, and keep the performer's head and feet in frame for 60% or more of the fight.
Cut at an average shot length of 1.5 to 3 s and build a fight from 4 to 8 short phrases of 2 to 5 s each.
Use slow motion at 48 to 96 fps for 1 to 3 s at the peak of a leap, a fall or a shot, then return to 24 fps.
Frame in 2.35:1 anamorphic with a 28mm to 50mm lens, and keep the camera at 0.5 to 1.5 m, moving at 1 to 3 m/s in a push, a whip or a spin.
Light with hard, coloured sources: a blue-green or sodium key at 4:1, with a smoke haze and neon in the back.
Do the dangerous stunt on set, with wire work or a real fall, and repeat the strike from two angles at 0.3 to 0.5 s apart.
Score with a synthesizer and a guitar theme, and add a punch, a whoosh and a shell casing to every hit.
anti_patterns: A static, wide master shot of a fight with no cut
A shaky, blurred close-up that hides the stunt
A stunt double hidden by an edit
A fight with no rhythm or slow-motion peak
A realistic, quiet sound track with no foley
A hero with no code of honour

composition.framing: A wide 2.35:1 frame in which the whole body and the weapon are readable; the fighters are on the lines of the frame.
composition.staging_in_depth: 3 planes: a foreground edge or a falling object, the fighters in the middle and a neon or a smoky back wall.
composition.subject_placement: Two fighters on opposite thirds; a hero in a long coat or a suit, in the centre third in the pause before a draw.

principles.rule: Build the fight from short phrases of strike and reply, and make the slow-motion peak the longest beat.
principles.value: 1.5 to 3 s average shot, 2 to 5 s per phrase

principles.rule: Aim a strike, a blade or a gun along a diagonal that crosses the 2.35:1 frame.
Put the two fighters on the opposite third lines and leave the centre for the clash.
Throw an object, a bottle or a shell casing through the foreground plane to give 3 layers.
principles.value: 3 planes, foreground object at 1 to 2 m

principles.rule: Set a hard coloured key against smoke and dark to make a clear silhouette.

camera_and_movement.movement: Push in on the draw, whip between fighters, spin 360° around a duel and follow a fall with a drop. Moves are fast and finish on a still beat.
camera_and_movement.support: Handheld, dolly, jib and a car or a boat mount; a wire rig for the performer
camera_and_movement.camera_height: 0.5 to 1.5 m; low for a leap, high for a fall
camera_and_movement.move_speed: 1 to 3 m/s for a push or a spin; whip pan 180° per second

lens_and_format.frame_rate: 24 fps; 48 to 96 fps for slow motion
lens_and_format.shutter_angle: 180° (1/48 s); 90° for a sharp, strobed strike
lens_and_format.focal_length: 28mm to 50mm (35mm format) for the body; 100mm for a gun close-up
lens_and_format.focus: A deep focus for a fight and a rack focus from a gun to a face over 0.5 to 1 s.

light.quality: Hard and coloured, with haze to show the beams, and a back light to rim the hero.
light.direction: From the side and behind, with a neon or a sodium lamp in the frame; a top light for the interrogation.
light.colour_temperature: Tungsten 3200K with blue gels at 7000K to 9000K and sodium at 2000K
light.source: Neon signs, sodium and tungsten with a haze machine

colour_and_grade.treatment: A saturated, slightly cool night look with blue-green shadows and amber neon; warm skin; clean, crisp blacks.
grade_recipe: Set the black point at 3% and keep deep, clean shadows.
Tint the shadows toward blue-green hue 190° at 20% to 30% strength.
Warm the highlights and skin to amber hue 35° at 10% strength.
Add a contrast curve of +25% and push saturation by +15% on neon and red.
Add grain at 10% and a halation of 4% to 6% around lamps.
colour_and_grade.texture: Medium grain at 10%, with halation and haze in the highlights

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 1.5 to 3 s in a fight (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 0.3 s for a hit to 8 s for a long take of a gunfight
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut on the impact and on the peak of a move. Show a strike from two angles at 0.3 to 0.5 s apart, and let a slow-motion beat stretch the climax.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut on impact, a speed ramp from 24 to 96 fps, a freeze frame of 1 s and a fast dissolve.

sound.approach: A post-dubbed track with large foley: each punch, whoosh, shell and bullet is a clear, loud event.
sound.dialogue: Dubbed, short and clipped, with a code-of-honour line before each fight.
sound.music: A synthesizer or a guitar theme with a strong melody, and a strings cue for a death; the music cuts at the strike.
sound.loudness: −20 LUFS integrated, with peaks at −2 dBFS for effects

titles_and_graphics.treatment: Bold titles that flash or slide on a freeze frame or a night skyline; credits roll over outtakes of the stunts.
titles_and_graphics.type: A bold gold or red sans-serif or a brush script in Chinese and English, 2 to 4 s on screen.

shot_primer.opening: Open on a hero in a long coat in a night street or a teahouse; the first strike or draw comes within 20 s.

positive: dove and shell casings in slow motion

canonical_works.work: Once Upon a Time in China

emotion.target_response: Thrill and admiration: the viewer sees the whole body in motion and feels the weight of each hit.

use_cases: music video with a fight scene
video prompts for a duel or a chase
avoid_when: The brief needs a quiet, observed or contemplative tone.
The piece cannot show the whole body, or has no space for a fight.

modifiers.how: Keep the speed of the action; shoot handheld at 24 fps with no slow motion, and let the camera lag behind the movement.
Keep the wide frame and the choreography; hold each fight in a single take of 60 s or more with no cut.

sources.title: Wikidata Q845641: Cinema of Hong Kong
Wikidata Q947446: Once Upon a Time in China
David Bordwell, Planet Hong Kong: Popular Cinema and the Art of Entertainment (Harvard University Press, 2000)
Stephen Teo, Hong Kong Cinema: The Extra Dimensions (BFI, 1997)
